intent: enterprise hooks: resolve Python via $PYTHON, unbreak Windows commits
notes: Fix Windows Python-not-found in the three global hook wrappers installed by `gator-enterprise activate`. Previously all three hardcoded `python3`, which on Windows resolves to a Microsoft Store App Execution Alias stub that "exists" on PATH but exits non-zero with an install prompt — the pre-commit / commit-msg / post-commit hooks failed silently on every Windows commit, blocking all governed activity. New `_PYTHON_RESOLVER` module-level constant is concatenated into each of `PRE_COMMIT_HOOK`, `COMMIT_MSG_HOOK`, `POST_COMMIT_HOOK` after the `GATOR_SCRIPT` existence check; resolves `$PYTHON` from (1) `~/.gator/enterprise/cli-python-path` (written by `_do_activate`, always present after activate), (2) `command -v python3`, (3) `command -v python`, else fails with clear stderr. All `python3` references in the three templates (final `--phase` invocation + inline `-c` mode-lookup + `POST_COMMIT_HOOK`'s `.gator/scripts/gator-session-block.py` fallback) now use `"$PYTHON"`. Added prominent TRIPWIRE header comment above the templates and a full `!` invariant to `.gator/charters/scripts-enterprise.md` with cross-reference to the parent plan artifact. Behavior on Linux/macOS is unchanged (they have `python3` on PATH; resolver falls through to it). Existing deployed wrappers get the fix on next `gator-enterprise activate --force`. Surfaced during the 2026-08-06 Enterprise Local Bring-Up plan (Session 2, Phase 5); documented in `.gator/vault/artifacts/2026-08-06-enterprise-local-bringup-session-log.md`.
